newsitem.title: USA: Rivlin says wage rise rate is relatively moderate.
newsitem.headline: Rivlin says wage rise rate is relatively moderate.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin said on Friday U.S. wages have been increasing, but at a moderate rate compared with past periods of equivalent unemployment.
"Wages have been increasing, especially recently, but actually fairly moderately compared to past periods when unemployment was this low," Rivlin said in a lecture at Widener University.

In a speech that largely repeated a talk she gave Thursday at the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School, Rivlin said various explanations have been advanced for the relative restraint in wage increases.
These explanations include worker insecurity due to company and government downsizing, a decline in trade union power, or increased mobility of companies to operate in low-wage areas, she said.
"The real question is, how long will it last?" she said. "If unemployment stays low, will wage increases begin to accelerate and how much?"
She repeated her characterization of the recent Federal Reserve rate hike as a "small insurance policy against the threat of future inflation."
